findings.title: Migration crashes when site_settings rows are missing
findings.body: Both `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` (line 11) and `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` (line 15) index into the result with `[0]` and immediately call `['id']`/`['value']` on it without checking whether any rows were returned. On a fresh install or any site where the `embed_category` setting was never customized (so no row exists in site_settings — site settings only persist a row once changed from default), `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire deploy. Only the `embeddable_hosts` query below is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0`; the other two need the same treatment.

findings.title: Migrated host values are not normalized, breaking the new lookup
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` site setting accepted values with scheme and path (the removed specs used values like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`), and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped schemes when comparing. The migration inserts these raw strings directly into `embeddable_hosts.host`, but the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against the bare URI hostname. Any previously configured host stored with a scheme or path will silently stop matching after this migration, so embedding from those sites stops working until an admin re-saves each host (only the model's `before_validation` strips the scheme). The migration should normalize values the same way the model does.

findings.title: SQL string interpolation of host values in migration
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the raw site-setting value straight into SQL. A host string containing a single quote will produce a SQL error (aborting the migration) or worse. Use `sanitize_sql_array` / quoted values instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: update/destroy crash when host id does not exist
findings.body: In both `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which does `host.host = ...` → NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil → NoMethodError. A request with a stale or invalid id returns a 500 instead of a 404. Both actions should raise `Discourse::NotFound` (or check `host.blank?`) when the record is missing.

findings.title: Category and embeddable_host fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category`. The contents of the two files were swapped by mistake. Fabrication loads every file in the fabricators directory so tests may still pass, but the files are misleadingly named and any tooling or developer looking for the category fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` (or relying on filename-to-fabricator conventions) will be confused; the definitions should live in their correctly named files.

findings.title: Case-sensitive host lookup can miss valid hosts
findings.body: `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but passes `uri.host` unmodified. The model's format validation allows uppercase (`/i`) and `before_validation` never downcases `host`, so a row saved as `Example.COM` (or a referer URI whose host contains uppercase) will never match because one side is lowercased and the other is not. Downcase both the stored host (in `before_validation`) and the lookup value to make matching consistent.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint/validation on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents duplicate `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host (no unique index in the migration, no `validates_uniqueness_of`). Admins can create several rows for the same hostname pointing at different categories, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so which category embedded topics land in is nondeterministic. Add a unique index on `host` and a uniqueness validation.
